strengths: Clear identification and empirical demonstration of a significant performance gap between foundation FM priors and domain-specific/untrained priors, well-motivated with clear tables and figures

Principled theoretical foundation using concentration-of-measure (Theorem 3.1) to motivate both warm-start strategy and sharp Gaussianity regularization; insightful critique of D-Flow's initialization lying in the S^c region
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple datasets (DIV2K, RealSR, AFHQ), four linear IP tasks, six evaluation metrics, and two scientific IPs with consistent improvements over baselines
Well-designed method combining time-dependent warm-start (Eq. 3.5) with explicit shell constraints (Eq. 3.7-3.9) instead of soft regularization, with closed-form projection operators
Natural extension to few-shot setting (Eq. 3.10) for scientific IPs with automatic instance selection via simplex constraint
Thorough ablation study (Table 6) validating both algorithmic components, with additional ablations on calibration effects in appendix
weaknesses: Limited theoretical rigor: Approximation error α_t ε in Eq. 3.4 lacks formal bounds; choice of α_t is heuristic without convergence guarantees; surjectivity of G_θ validated only empirically (Table 2), not theoretically

Fairness concerns in experimental comparisons: FMPlug inherently advantages from assumptions (simple-distortion) that D-Flow doesn't assume; FMPlug uses y directly (Eq. 3.5), providing privileged information; comparing across interleaving vs. plug-in paradigms conflates approaches

Generalization gaps: All experiments use only Stable Diffusion V3; no results on Flux.1 or other foundation models mentioned in introduction; limited to image domain with no exploration of other modalities

Missing ablations and sensitivity analyses: Shell parameter ε=0.025 unchosen without justification or sensitivity study; hyperparameter sensitivity (learning rates 0.5 for z, 0.005 for t) not explored; no analysis of learned t values across tasks
Computational cost underreported: Wall-clock time comparisons absent; mean-variance calibration overhead (4000 samples) not quantified; efficiency gains from shorter flows not demonstrated

Few-shot results remain far from domain-specific methods: Table 5 shows 2.72 PSNR gap to Red-Diff on LIS and 5.45 on MRI; only two scientific IP tasks tested; unclear when FMPlug is preferable to domain-specific priors given few-shot requirement
Gaussian assumption not validated: No investigation of how model training errors or FM architecture variations affect intermediate distribution Gaussianity
Performance on no-reference metrics (CLIPIQA/MUSIQ): FMPlug not best on these metrics (Table 3), raising questions about visual quality improvements

Reproducibility concerns: No code release mentioned; model-specific mean-variance pre-computation required; hyperparameter choices lack justification; dimension handling for scientific IPs (channel replication) appears ad-hoc

strengths: Addresses a practically relevant gap: demonstrates that foundation FM priors significantly underperform compared to domain-specific or untrained priors, and this problem deserves attention
Well-grounded theoretical motivation using concentration-of-measure results to explain why D-Flow's initialization is problematic
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple datasets (DIV2K, RealSR, AFHQ, LIS, MRI) with diverse metrics (PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, CLIPIQA, MUSIQ)
Elegant and computationally convenient methodology with closed-form projection for the shell constraint
Useful ablation study demonstrating contributions of warm-start and Gaussian regularization components
Consistent improvements over D-Flow baseline across multiple tasks
weaknesses: Critical: Core approximation in Eq. (3.4) lacks mathematical rigor—dropping αtε by claiming 'appropriate αt can make it sufficiently small' is vague and unquantified; no error bounds provided and potential error accumulation during optimization not analyzed

Limited novelty: primarily combines known techniques (concentration-of-measure results, shell constraints from Yang et al. 2024, standard warm-start strategies) without significant new theoretical insights

Weak justification for surjectivity assumption: image regression test (Table 2) on identity mapping doesn't prove surjectivity for general inverse problems; LPIPS difference of 0.088 is substantial

Insufficient parameter sensitivity analysis: ε=0.025 choice is unjustified and arbitrary; learning rate choices (0.5 for z, 0.005 for t) lack explanation; no ablation studies on critical hyperparameters

Inconsistent perceptual quality: FMPlug often achieves lower CLIPIQA/MUSIQ (no-reference metrics) scores than competitors, suggesting overfitting to PSNR/SSIM while potentially worse actual visual quality—not addressed

Limited generalization: only tested on Stable Diffusion V3; applicability to Flux.1 and other foundation models unclear; performance with pixel-space FM models unknown
No failure case analysis or discussion of when method degrades, and how it handles images significantly different from training distribution

strengths: Clear identification and empirical validation of a significant performance gap between foundation FM priors and domain-specific/untrained alternatives, with concrete evidence (Table 1, Figure 2)
Theoretically motivated approach using concentration-of-measure results to explain initialization problems in prior work and design improved solutions (Section 3.1)
Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple datasets (DIV2K, RealSR, AFHQ), tasks (4 IP types), metrics (6+ evaluation measures), and settings (simple-distortion, few-shot)
Strong empirical results with FMPlug consistently outperforming foundation FM baselines and substantially narrowing the gap to domain-specific priors (Tables 3-4, Figures 4-8)
Practical significance for enabling deployment of foundation models in inverse problems without domain-specific training
Clear presentation with good intuitions, helpful visualizations (Figures 1, 3), and detailed reproducibility information

weaknesses: Incomplete theoretical analysis: approximation error α_t ε in Eq. (3.4) lacks rigorous bounds; no convergence analysis for optimization problems; shell constraint effectiveness is intuitive but lacks formal guarantees on impact

Missing ablation on shell constraint design choices: hard vs. soft regularization comparison absent; why shell is better than spherical constraint ||z||₂=√d not justified
Limited applicability scope not clearly discussed: method requires either x≈y (simple-distortion) or K reference samples (few-shot); no analysis of failure modes or settings where method struggles

strengths: Well-motivated problem: Clearly demonstrates the performance gap between foundation FM, domain-specific, and untrained priors for inverse problems (Tables 1, 2-3), an important issue not previously explicitly highlighted
Sound theoretical grounding: Uses concentration-of-measure theory to explain why existing warm-start strategies fail, providing clear intuition for the proposed approach
Insightful regularization analysis: Figure 4 effectively demonstrates why D-Flow's Gaussian regularization is ineffective, motivating the sharp shell constraint solution with closed-form projection

Comprehensive experimental validation: 12 simple-distortion scenarios, 3 scientific imaging problems, clear ablations, robustness analysis across random initializations, and sensitivity studies demonstrating methodological rigor
Practical relevance for scientific imaging: Well-motivated extension to few-shot setting addresses real barriers (data/training costs) to developing domain-specific models in scientific domains
Strong reproducibility: Complete algorithms, detailed hyperparameters, implementation details for all baselines, and use of standard datasets facilitate reproduction
Clear and well-organized presentation: Good use of illustrations (especially Figures 1 and 4) to convey key ideas; logical progression from problem motivation to solutions
weaknesses: Surjectivity assumption not theoretically proven: Reliance on image regression test with only 1000 DIV2K images (Table 2) is insufficient to establish approximate surjectivity across diverse domains; potential failure modes on out-of-distribution data are not adequately addressed

Significant performance gaps in scientific IPs: MRI reconstruction shows large gap vs. domain-specific priors (23.60 vs. 28.71 PSNR, Table 4); explanation involving spatial variability mismatch undermines strong claims, suggesting method may not generalize to all scientific domains

Theoretical gaps in warm-start justification: Approximation in Eq. 3.4 assumes αtε is controllable but αt is learned, creating circularity; no formal analysis of how approximation error affects solution quality; learnable t is pragmatic but lacks convergence guarantees

Moderate novelty: Individual components (spherical constraints, warm-start strategies, Gaussian regularization) are not new; contribution primarily lies in their combination for this application, making the work somewhat incremental

Computational cost not adequately justified: Table 9 shows FMPlug (492s) is ~50-70× slower than interleaving methods (7-10s) though better quality than DIP; efficiency gains over D-Flow (456s) are marginal while requiring more complex optimization

CLIPIQA/MUSIQ metric underperformance unexplained: FMPlug consistently underperforms on no-reference metrics (Table 3), dismissed in appendix due to general metric robustness concerns; selective failure on these metrics deserves investigation rather than dismissal

Experimental fairness concerns: Different methods use different NFEs (3-28), D-Flow compared against with different optimizer (AdamW vs. LBFGS), 100 images per dataset is limited sample size, and no error bars/significance tests on main results

Few-shot assumptions and limitations: Method requires instances close to target x; MRI failure case (Figure 8) shows limitations when instances lack spatial diversity; simplex constraint w∈ΔK lacks ablation studies
Limited scope: Only addresses image inverse problems; applicability to video, 3D, or non-image modalities unclear, limiting the generality of contributions

Theoretical aspects of optimization: No analysis of how shell constraint tightness ε affects optimization landscape, convergence properties, or why particular parameterization (learnable t via sigmoid) is optimal

strengths: Identifies an important empirical gap: foundation FM priors significantly underperform domain-specific and untrained priors on inverse problems, which is well-documented and valuable for the community
Provides theoretical motivation using concentration-of-measure theory to explain problematic initialization, offering useful intuition about why standard approaches fail
Comprehensive experimental evaluation spanning multiple datasets (DIV2K, RealSR, AFHQ), diverse tasks (super-resolution, inpainting, deblurring), multiple metrics, and thorough ablation studies
Well-articulated motivation for scientific IPs where domain-specific models are prohibitively expensive, with a practical few-shot extension addressing real constraints
Clear presentation with effective motivation, illustrations, and readable exposition of the problem and approach
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: warm-start strategy is simply making t learnable (not fundamentally new), and Gaussian regularization via shell constraints is similar to Yang et al. (2024), making the core contributions incremental rather than novel

Weak theoretical justification: concentration-of-measure argument (Theorem 3.1) doesn't rigorously support that Gθ only operates on shell S; neural networks typically generalize beyond training domains, and no theoretical guarantee that modifications improve convergence

Overclaimed gap closure: Table 16 shows FMPlug(FD) achieves 29.00 PSNR vs FMPlug(DS) 27.44 on Gaussian blur; scientific IPs show MRI gap of 5.1 dB vs domain-specific (23.60 vs 28.71), contradicting the 'saving' framing in title

Unfair computational comparisons: FMPlug uses NFE=3 while D-Flow uses NFE=6 and FlowDPS/FlowChef use NFE=28; Table 9 shows FMPlug is 49x slower than FlowDPS (492s vs 10s), making performance claims less convincing without matching budgets

Restrictive and often-violated assumptions: simple-distortion setting requires x≈y (limiting applicability); few-shot setting requires similar samples; MRI results explicitly show assumptions are violated (test instances don't match guidance), yet method still underperforms

Scientific IP experiments are limited: only 3 of 5 InverseBench tasks used, MRI gap relative to domain-specific methods is substantial, and weak correlation analysis suggests the method identifies similar instances but still substantially underperforms

Inconsistent performance on no-reference metrics: FMPlug doesn't consistently win on CLIPIQA and MUSIQ; dismissal as 'unreliable' (Appendix A.4) seems ad-hoc and raises evaluation credibility concerns

Insufficient justification for hyperparameter choices: ε=0.025 chosen empirically without principled guidance; limited sensitivity analysis; no explanation for why softmax weighting or other design choices are optimal

Reproducibility concerns: code not mentioned as available, project page not linked, dimension-mismatch handling underspecified, and some hyperparameters appear problem-specific without general guidance
Image regression test (Table 2) is weak evidence for surjectivity: only 1000 images and marginal improvement (36.19 vs 37.92 PSNR) don't rigorously establish that all natural images are representable

strengths: Identifies and quantifies an important practical problem: foundation FM priors significantly underperform domain-specific and untrained priors for solving IPs, with clear experimental evidence (Table 1, Figs. 2-3)
Theoretically motivated approach using concentration-of-measure results to explain why existing initialization fails and justify the time-dependent warm-start strategy
Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple datasets (DIV2K, AFHQ, RealSR), tasks (4 linear IPs), metrics (6 metrics), and thorough ablation studies demonstrating necessity of components
Strong empirical results: FMPlug achieves consistent improvements over D-Flow baseline and approaches domain-specific FM performance, particularly valuable for scientific IPs with few samples
Novel extension to few-shot setting for scientific IPs addresses real practical constraints (cost of data collection and model training) in scientific imaging domains
Excellent reproducibility: detailed algorithms, hyperparameters, complete results, and robustness analysis (Table 17 shows remarkably low variance)
Well-motivated problem identification and clear presentation of motivation, intuition, and empirical validation
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: warm-start is straightforward (learnable time parameter), shell constraints for Gaussianity are from Yang et al. 2024; primary contribution is combination rather than fundamental new techniques

Theoretical gaps: connection between CoM (Theorem 3.1) and practical performance is intuitive but not rigorously established; surjectivity claim (Table 2) based on limited empirical evidence (1000 images); no convergence analysis for non-convex joint optimization in Eq. 3.7

Few-shot setting assumptions violated in practice: for MRI, spatial concentration of instances causes large performance gap (23.60 vs 28.71 PSNR for Red-Diff); assumption that instances are close to unknown x may not hold universally
Severe computational cost: FMPlug ~50-70× slower than interleaving methods (492s vs 7-10s, Table 9), limiting practical applicability despite superior quality; no analysis of quality-speed tradeoffs
Inconsistent performance on no-reference metrics: CLIPIQA/MUSIQ often underperform (sometimes by 0.1-0.3), and dismissing these metrics as unreliable feels defensive when they are widely used

Incomplete hyperparameter guidance: ε=0.025 based on limited sensitivity analysis (3 values); learning rates appear dataset-dependent without principled generalization strategy; no guidance for new problems
